h1: Hop Inn Phitsanulok — clean rooms at an easy price, in town on Mittraphap Road
intro: If you want a place in Phitsanulok that just delivers a clean room, a comfortable bed and a low price with no frills, Hop Inn Phitsanulok on Mittraphap Road is the kind of choice frequent travellers book without overthinking. It is a 2-star budget hotel by Hop Inn (Erawan Group) with 79 rooms that follows the same formula at every branch: clean standard rooms, consistent pricing and free parking. It sits on Mittraphap Road near Central Phitsanulok, Chaloem Phrakiat Park and Big C, with easy access in and out of town. Rooms start from around ฿790/night.

body.html: Hop Inn Phitsanulok on Mittraphap Road is one branch of Erawan Group's Hop Inn chain, which is spread across Thailand's secondary cities. The brand's pitch is clear from the start: clean standard rooms at a fixed, honest price, with nothing that inflates the bill. It's a multi-storey building with a lift and 79 rooms, designed to be plain and easy to use. People driving through Phitsanulok, here for work, or stopping overnight before continuing on to Sukhothai or Loei tend to pick it because they know exactly what they're getting — no surprises.

Standard rooms are about 20 sqm and come as a Double or a Twin. Inside you get air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, a work desk and a hot-water shower. What guests say most often is that the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable and everything looks new — many reviews say it's cleaner than the price suggests. The trade-off is that the rooms really are plain: no decoration, no bathtub and no in-house breakfast. It's a good bedroom at a good price, not a place to hang out in all day.
"Very clean room, comfortable bed, smiling staff and plenty of parking. For this price in town it's genuinely good value — perfect for a one-night stop before moving on."

Service is another point that scores better than you'd expect from a budget hotel. Staff are praised for being friendly and helpful, the front desk is open 24 hours, and there's CCTV and security that guests say make them feel at ease. The free private parking is fairly spacious, which is a real convenience for self-drivers. There's a small in-house eatery for simple meals, but no full breakfast buffet like a bigger hotel — the upside is that food shops and convenience stores are an easy walk away.

The Mittraphap Road location makes getting in and out of town easy. It's close to Central Phitsanulok, Chaloem Phrakiat Park and Big C, all a few minutes by car. Phitsanulok Walking Street is about 2 km away, and Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai), home of the revered Phra Phuttha Chinnarat, is roughly 10 minutes by car. Phitsanulok Airport is about 20 minutes away. The overall score sits around 9.4 from 93 reviews on Trip.com and around 8.8 on Booking.com, with cleanliness, location and value rated highest.

To be honest, Hop Inn has no atmosphere or view to speak of, and it isn't in the riverside Wat Yai quarter. Some guests note the rooms aren't fully soundproof — you can hear the corridor or the next room at times — and the main-road location means you'll drive or grab a ride to reach the Nan River sightseeing area. If you want a riverside boutique feel or to walk to Wat Yai, Dragon River Avenue or Fortune D may suit you better. But if you want a clean room, a comfortable night's sleep, free parking and the lowest easy price in town, this place does the job — reliably.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a higher floor away from the corridor or common areas to cut down on noise. If you're driving, the free on-site parking is a real advantage in town. Booking direct through the Hop Inn app can be cheaper at times, but always compare with Agoda and Booking first. And since there's no breakfast here, plan to head out for riverside dangling-leg noodles or other morning food in town.

The brand's cleanliness and consistency are genuine strengths — just accept that the rooms are plain, there's no breakfast, and the main-road location isn't in the riverside Wat Yai quarter.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Hop Inn Phitsanulok

faq.q: Where is Hop Inn Phitsanulok, and what's nearby?
faq.a: This branch sits at 999/119 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, in central Phitsanulok. It's near Chaloem Phrakiat Park (about a 5-minute walk) and Big C. Central Phitsanulok is about 7 minutes by car, Phitsanulok Walking Street is roughly 2 km away, and Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) is about 10 minutes by car. Phitsanulok Airport is around 20 minutes away.

faq.q: How much does Hop Inn Phitsanulok cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from around ฿790/night for a Standard Double of about 20 sqm. There's also a Standard Twin (two single beds) at a similar rate. During long weekends or festivals, rates rise to around ฿950-990 and rooms fill quickly. Prices vary by season and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Hop Inn Phitsanulok best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who want a clean room, a comfortable night's sleep, an easy price and free parking. It suits self-drivers passing through Phitsanulok, people here for work, or anyone stopping overnight before continuing to Sukhothai or Loei who values consistency and value over atmosphere or a river view.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Hop Inn clean and quiet?
faq.a: Cleanliness is the point guests praise most — clean, new-looking rooms with comfortable beds, and many reviews say it's cleaner than the price suggests. However, the rooms aren't fully soundproof, so you can hear the corridor or the next room at times. It's best to request a higher floor away from common areas and pack ear plugs to be safe.

faq.q: Does it have parking and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes to free private parking, which is fairly spacious and very convenient for self-drivers. However, there's no breakfast buffet — only a small in-house eatery for simple meals. The upside is that food shops and convenience stores are an easy walk away for breakfast.

faq.q: What chain is Hop Inn, and is it reliable?
faq.a: Hop Inn is a budget hotel chain by Erawan Group, with many branches across Thailand's secondary cities. Its strength is a consistent clean-room standard and steady pricing at every branch. This Mittraphap Road branch scores around 9.4 from 93 reviews on Trip.com and around 8.8 on Booking.com, with cleanliness, location and value rated highest.
